newsitem.title: USA: California floods set to become state's most costly.
newsitem.headline: California floods set to become state's most costly.

text.p: Losses from California's New Year floods doubled to more than $1.5 billion on Tuesday and the floods looked set to become the most costly in the state's history, officials said.
Severe floods in California have killed six people, damaged thousands of homes and inundated tens of thousands of acres of prime farmland.

Authorities asked 4,000 people to evacuate their homes near the town of Manteca in central California, where two new levee breaks along the bloated San Joaquin River flooded thousands of acres of farmland on Tuesday, officials said.
Elsewhere, workers battled to shore up fragile levees.

In Sacramento, California Gov. Pete Wilson called for a special session of the state legislature "to address the clear and immediate needs of those individuals, businesses and farms victimised by those terrible floods."

Receding waters allowed evacuees in some areas to return to their homes to clean up, but officials warned that they faced hazards from raw sewage, dead animals and chemicals that may have contaminated the water.

Health officials recommended that flood victims discard any food that might have come into contact with floodwater and wear rubber boots and waterproof gloves during cleanup if there had been a backflow of sewage in their house.

The California Office of Emergency Services said 19 counties and one city had reported damage from the floods estimated at more than $1.5 billion. Losses included $661 million of damage to homes and businesses and $902 million of damage to infrastructure such as roads and bridges.
The total doubled from the $775 million in damage reported by nine counties and one city on Monday.

But 23 of the counties where Wilson has declared states of emergency have not yet reported damage and officials said this year's floods were almost certain to overtake 1995 floods as the most damaging in state history. The 1995 floods caused $1.8 billion of damage.

President Bill Clinton has declared a major disaster in parts of California, Nevada and Idaho due to storms and floods that hit the West in the last 10 days. Oregon and Washington also suffered widespread damage from floods and landslides that have killed at least 20 people in the region.
